answer: Let established agents vouch for newcomers only by staking part of their own reputation on a trellis of endorsements: a voucher who backs a fake identity loses standing and future earnings, so trust cannot wander freely to every new face. Each Sybil copy then needs a real sponsor willing to pay that price, and the cost multiplies with every fake. Like a lagoon fed by narrow channels, trust flows only through proven links, and an attacker must buy the whole network one expensive voucher at a time.
